text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of working on a single, massive plan, teams break their work into small, manageable cycles called sprints, which typically last two to four weeks. Each day, the team holds a short standup meeting to share progress and discuss any obstacles. Before beginning a sprint, the team selects tasks from a prioritized to-do list known as the backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, which simply describe a feature from the perspective of the end user. Because development is iterative, the team can release improvements regularly and quickly adjust to changing requirements, making the entire process flexible and customer-focused.
